sourceTypes.niro: Defined by Niro original sources (audio / risk-logic sheet / brief consolidating them)
sourceTypes.external: Externally verified against authoritative medical source (org+URL recorded)
sourceTypes.needs-clarification: Not resolvable from Niro sources or trusted external sources without ambiguity

legend.niroScoringNote: Per-parameter scoring thresholds & points are defined in the Niro Risk Logic Google Sheet, which is referenced by the Niro brief but NOT present in the provided folder. Every niroScoring block is therefore status=needs-clarification until the sheet is provided. External clinical bands below are clearly-labelled interpretation references, NOT substitutes for Niro scoring.
legend.validationNote: validation.min/max are engineering plausibility guards for input sanity (soft warn / hard block), not medical claims. Tune during implementation.

biomarkers.whatItMeasures: Total cholesterol across LDL, HDL and other lipoprotein fractions.
biomarkers.whyItMatters: Elevated levels drive atherosclerosis, raising coronary artery disease, heart attack and stroke risk.

niroScoring.note: Await Niro Risk Logic Sheet points/thresholds

sources.title: Cholesterol Levels: What You Need to Know

sources.ref: Niro brief §5 — parameter of Cardiovascular domain

biomarkers.whatItMeasures: Cholesterol carried by high-density lipoproteins (reverse transport to the liver).
biomarkers.whyItMatters: Higher HDL is protective; low HDL is an independent cardiovascular risk factor.

referenceExternal.conflict: StatPearls female low cutoff <55 vs MedlinePlus/NCEP <50 — recorded, not merged

biomarkers.whatItMeasures: Cholesterol carried by low-density lipoproteins.
biomarkers.whyItMatters: Primary atherogenic particle; lower is better.

sources.title: LDL: The Bad Cholesterol
sources.note: NCEP ATP III tiers verified verbatim

biomarkers.whatItMeasures: Most common type of fat in the blood (fasting sample, 9–12h).
biomarkers.whyItMatters: High levels raise coronary artery disease risk; very high levels risk acute pancreatitis.

biomarkers.whatItMeasures: Arterial pressure when the heart contracts.
biomarkers.whyItMatters: Leading modifiable risk factor for heart attack, stroke, heart failure and kidney disease.

referenceExternal.note: 2017 ACC/AHA categories; retained by 2025 AHA/ACC guideline. Full classification also uses diastolic — Niro brief lists systolic only.

sources.ref: Niro brief §5 — systolic BP is the listed CV parameter

biomarkers.whatItMeasures: Very low CRP concentrations, used for cardiovascular risk stratification.
biomarkers.whyItMatters: Low-grade vascular inflammation predicts atherosclerotic cardiovascular events.

sources.title: Pearson et al., Circulation 2003;107:499–511
sources.note: publisher fetch blocked; values verified via NIH-family sources

biomarkers.whatItMeasures: Balance of atherogenic (ApoB) vs anti-atherogenic (ApoA-I) lipoprotein particles.
biomarkers.whyItMatters: Higher ratio predicts major adverse cardiovascular events decades in advance (AMORIS cohort).

referenceExternal.note: RESEARCH-DERIVED (AMORIS/PLOS Medicine 2021), not guideline-defined. No US clinical guideline categories exist.

niroScoring.note: Niro sheet may define its own bands — must take precedence over research-derived bands

sources.note: Guideline-grade categories do not exist; flag in UI as research-derived

biomarkers.whatItMeasures: Blood glucose after ≥8 hour fast.
biomarkers.whyItMatters: ADA diagnostic test for prediabetes and diabetes.

biomarkers.whatItMeasures: Percent of hemoglobin with attached glucose ≈ 3-month average blood glucose.
biomarkers.whyItMatters: Diagnostic + long-term glycemic control standard; higher A1C correlates with complications.

referenceExternal.note: ADA categories, verified on ADA + NIDDK

biomarkers.whatItMeasures: Insulin concentration after 8–12h fast; HOMA-IR input.
biomarkers.whyItMatters: Assesses insulin resistance and hypoglycemia causes.

referenceExternal.note: No universal guideline range; assays not standardized. MedlinePlus provides no numbers; URMC free-insulin '<17 µIU/mL' with lab-variation caveat. Do not hard-code a range without the user's lab interval or the Niro sheet.

sources.note: Range must come from Niro sheet or user's lab report

biomarkers.whatItMeasures: Derived value converting HbA1c into meter units (mg/dL).
biomarkers.whyItMatters: Relates 3-month A1C to daily glucose readings.

referenceExternal.note: No independent categories — interpret via HbA1c bands.

niroScoring.note: Confirm whether Niro scores eAG separately or uses it as display-only

sources.ref: Niro brief §5 lists eAG as a Metabolic parameter

biomarkers.whatItMeasures: Pro-inflammatory cytokine that drives the acute-phase response (induces CRP).
biomarkers.whyItMatters: Rises early in infection, sepsis and systemic inflammation.

referenceExternal.note: Assay/lab-dependent; no guideline categories. Interpret against the performing lab's interval.

sources.title: Said et al. 2021 — IL-6 in healthy individuals (meta-analysis)

biomarkers.whatItMeasures: Hepatic acute-phase protein; general inflammation marker.
biomarkers.whyItMatters: Detects/monitors infection and inflammatory disease (RA, lupus, IBD).

referenceExternal.note: StatPearls interpretation bands converted from mg/dL to mg/L (×10)

biomarkers.whatItMeasures: RBC settling distance in one hour (Westergren); indirect inflammation marker.
biomarkers.whyItMatters: Detects/monitors inflammatory conditions; not diagnostic alone.

referenceExternal.note: Miller age rule (M: age/2, F: (age+10)/2) available as rule-of-thumb (BMJ 1983) — label as such if used

biomarkers.whatItMeasures: Serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D — the accepted vitamin D status indicator.
biomarkers.whyItMatters: Deficiency impairs calcium absorption (rickets/osteomalacia); excess risks toxicity.

referenceExternal.note: NIH ODS/FNB framework (current). CONFLICT: Endocrine Society 2011 used <20 deficient / 21–29 insufficient / ≥30 sufficient; ES 2024 guideline no longer endorses thresholds. Surface both, label by framework.

sources.title: Vitamin D — Health Professional Fact Sheet, Table 1

biomarkers.whatItMeasures: Serum B12 — cofactor for DNA synthesis, RBC formation, neurological function.
biomarkers.whyItMatters: Deficiency causes megaloblastic anemia and potentially irreversible neurological damage.

referenceExternal.conflict: ODS subnormal <200–250 vs MedlinePlus normal floor 299 — recorded, both displayed

sources.title: Vitamin B12 — Health Professional Fact Sheet

biomarkers.whatItMeasures: Circulating folate (recent intake; RBC folate = long-term status).
biomarkers.whyItMatters: Deficiency causes megaloblastic anemia; low folate raises neural tube defect risk in pregnancy.

referenceExternal.conflict: WHO metabolic-indicator deficiency <4 ng/mL; ODS adequacy >3 ng/mL; MedlinePlus normal 2.7–17.0 — all recorded

biomarkers.whatItMeasures: Main iron-storage protein; proxy for body iron stores (acute-phase caveat).
biomarkers.whyItMatters: Most efficient single test for iron deficiency; also flags iron overload.

referenceExternal.conflict: WHO deficiency <15 µg/L (epidemiological) vs NIH ODS <30 µg/L (clinical suggestion) — both recorded; with inflammation WHO uses <70 (adults)

sources.title: Guideline on use of ferritin concentrations (2020)

biomarkers.whatItMeasures: Serum magnesium (<1% of body stores — imperfect status marker).
biomarkers.whyItMatters: Cofactor in 300+ enzyme systems; low levels disturb neuromuscular and cardiac function.

referenceExternal.conflict: ODS 0.75–0.95 mmol/L (≈1.82–2.31 mg/dL, hypomagnesemia <0.75 mmol/L) vs MedlinePlus 1.7–2.2 mg/dL (0.70–0.91 mmol/L) — overlapping but different; both recorded

biomarkers.whatItMeasures: Serum/plasma zinc — most common status proxy (no gold standard).
biomarkers.whyItMatters: Required for immunity, wound healing, protein/DNA synthesis, growth.

referenceExternal.note: SINGLE-SOURCE anchor (NIH ODS only) — no WHO/MedlinePlus cross-check found; ODS cautions serum zinc is imperfect

biomarkers.whatItMeasures: Hepatocyte enzyme released on liver-cell injury; most liver-specific aminotransferase.
biomarkers.whyItMatters: Primary hepatocellular injury screen; elevated ALT associates with liver-related mortality.

referenceExternal.conflict: ACG 2017 true-normal ULN: M 29–33, F 19–25 IU/L (sex-specific) vs typical lab 4–36 — both recorded. ACG elevation magnitudes: <2× / 2–5× / 5–15× / >15× ULN.

sources.title: ACG Clinical Guideline: Evaluation of Abnormal Liver Chemistries (2017) — summary PDF

biomarkers.whatItMeasures: Enzyme in liver plus heart/muscle/kidney/brain/RBC; less liver-specific than ALT.
biomarkers.whyItMatters: Interpreted with ALT to characterize liver injury; AST>ALT pattern suggests alcohol-related disease.

referenceExternal.conflict: MedlinePlus 8–33 vs StatPearls 5–30 U/L — both recorded; no guideline sex-specific AST ULN

biomarkers.whatItMeasures: Liver/biliary membrane enzyme; rises with cholestasis, alcohol and many drugs.
biomarkers.whyItMatters: Confirms hepatic origin of elevated ALP; not a standalone screening test (ACG).

referenceExternal.conflict: UMich MLabs sex-specific (verified) vs MedlinePlus 5–40 (unisex) vs StatPearls 6–50 — all recorded; Mayo M 8–61 unverified (403)

biomarkers.whatItMeasures: Heme-breakdown pigment (conjugated + unconjugated).
biomarkers.whyItMatters: Elevations indicate hemolysis, hepatocellular disease or biliary obstruction.

referenceExternal.conflict: MedlinePlus 0.1–1.2 vs StatPearls ≈0.12–1.0 mg/dL — both recorded

biomarkers.whatItMeasures: Most abundant plasma protein (hepatic synthesis); oncotic balance + transport.
biomarkers.whyItMatters: Marker of hepatic synthetic function and nutritional/inflammatory state.

referenceExternal.conflict: MedlinePlus 3.4–5.4 vs StatPearls 3.5–5.0 g/dL — both recorded. Severity grading: needs-clarification (no official bands)

biomarkers.whatItMeasures: Estimated kidney filtration rate (CKD-EPI, from creatinine ± cystatin C, age, sex).
biomarkers.whyItMatters: Primary marker for detecting and staging chronic kidney disease.

referenceExternal.note: KDIGO stages via NKF (verified); G1/G2 are CKD only with kidney damage ≥3 months

sources.title: eGFR test — kidney function levels & stages

biomarkers.whatItMeasures: Muscle-metabolism waste product cleared by the kidneys; eGFR input.
biomarkers.whyItMatters: Elevated creatinine indicates impaired kidney function.

referenceExternal.conflict: MedlinePlus M 0.7–1.3 / F 0.5–0.95 vs StatPearls M 0.6–1.2 / F 0.5–1.1 — both recorded

biomarkers.whatItMeasures: Urea nitrogen from protein breakdown (liver produces, kidneys excrete).
biomarkers.whyItMatters: Kidney function check; rises with impairment, dehydration, high catabolism.

referenceExternal.conflict: MedlinePlus 6–20 vs Clinical Methods 5–20 mg/dL — both recorded

biomarkers.whatItMeasures: End product of purine metabolism.
biomarkers.whyItMatters: Hyperuricemia underlies gout and urate stones; associated with kidney disease.

referenceExternal.conflict: Clinical hyperuricemia >6 (F) / >7 (M) mg/dL (StatPearls) sits BELOW lab reference upper bounds — reference interval ≠ clinical threshold; both displayed

biomarkers.whatItMeasures: Pituitary hormone driving thyroid hormone production; most sensitive thyroid index.
biomarkers.whyItMatters: High TSH → hypothyroidism; low TSH → hyperthyroidism.

referenceExternal.conflict: Upper limit: 4.0 (ATA 2014, PMC-verified) vs 4.5 (StatPearls/USPSTF) vs 4.8 (MedlinePlus) — all recorded; TSH runs higher in age >80

biomarkers.whatItMeasures: Unbound (biologically available) thyroxine.
biomarkers.whyItMatters: With TSH, distinguishes overt from subclinical thyroid dysfunction.

referenceExternal.conflict: MedlinePlus 0.8–1.9 vs Cleveland Clinic 0.9–1.7 ng/dL — both recorded (assay-dependent)

biomarkers.whatItMeasures: Unbound triiodothyronine — the most metabolically active thyroid hormone.
biomarkers.whyItMatters: Evaluates hyperthyroidism (incl. T3 toxicosis); clarifies TSH/FT4 patterns.

referenceExternal.conflict: MedlinePlus 2.1–4.4 vs Cleveland Clinic 2.3–4.1 pg/mL — both recorded

biomarkers.whatItMeasures: IgG autoantibodies against thyroid peroxidase (autoimmune thyroid disease).
biomarkers.whyItMatters: High levels signal Hashimoto's; positivity predicts future hypothyroidism risk.

referenceExternal.note: STRONGLY lab/assay-dependent — negative/positive per performing lab's cutoff; no universal threshold

biomarkers.whatItMeasures: Oxygen-carrying protein concentration in whole blood.
biomarkers.whyItMatters: Defines anemia (fatigue, impaired oxygen delivery) and polycythemia when high.

referenceExternal.note: WHO 2024 cutoffs verified from guideline PDF; severity: mild/moderate/severe at 110–129(M)/110–119(F), 80–109, <80 g/L

sources.title: Guideline on haemoglobin cutoffs to define anaemia (2024)

biomarkers.whatItMeasures: Average red blood cell volume.
biomarkers.whyItMatters: Classifies anemia (microcytic/normocytic/macrocytic), steering the workup.

referenceExternal.conflict: StatPearls 80–100 (standard clinical classification) vs MedlinePlus 79–95 fL — both recorded

biomarkers.whatItMeasures: Total white blood cells per volume of blood.
biomarkers.whyItMatters: High = infection/inflammation/malignancy signal; low = marrow suppression, infection risk.

biomarkers.whatItMeasures: Platelet count per volume of blood.
biomarkers.whyItMatters: Low = bleeding risk; high = reactive states or myeloproliferative disease.

referenceExternal.conflict: Upper normal: MedlinePlus 400 vs StatPearls 450 ×10⁹/L (current hematology practice) — both recorded. Severity: mild 100–150, moderate 50–100, severe <50

biomarkers.whatItMeasures: Adrenal glucocorticoid — strongly time-of-day dependent (peak early morning).
biomarkers.whyItMatters: Detects abnormal production (Cushing syndrome, adrenal insufficiency).

referenceExternal.conflict: MedlinePlus 5–25 (8 a.m.) vs Cleveland Clinic 10–20 (6–8 a.m.) µg/dL — both recorded. Draw-time capture REQUIRED (context rule).

niroScoring.note: Niro brief §6 documents context-specific handling for hormonal measurements

biomarkers.whatItMeasures: Total testosterone in blood (both sexes produce it).
biomarkers.whyItMatters: Low in men → hypogonadism symptoms; elevated in women → PCOS workup.

bands.label: Low-T threshold (AUA)
bands.note: supports diagnosis with symptoms, 2 early-morning draws

referenceExternal.conflict: Low-T cutoff: AUA 300 (verified) vs Endocrine Society 264 ng/dL (harmonized range verified; diagnostic use search-verified) — both displayed, labeled by organization

sources.title: Evaluation and Management of Testosterone Deficiency

biomarkers.whatItMeasures: Most potent estrogen; dominant during female reproductive years.
biomarkers.whyItMatters: Evaluates ovarian function, fertility, menopausal status; gynecomastia workup in men.

referenceExternal.note: Menstrual-phase-specific ranges: NEEDS CLARIFICATION — no verifiable universal phase table (Mayo catalog blocked); phase interpretation is lab-report-dependent
referenceExternal.contextRequirement: sex + menopausal status (+ cycle phase if lab-provided)
